name: Fujitsu Tofu Interconnect 2
description: Fujitsu’s second-generation Tofu interconnect retained the six-dimensional mesh/torus design and integrated the controller into the FX100 node processor. It was used in the National Institute for Fusion Science’s updated Plasma Simulator.

date.basis: The Hot Interconnects presentation deck gives the day.

events.statement: Fujitsu's team presented the Tofu2 interconnect design, integrating the network controller into the processor chip while retaining the six-dimensional mesh/torus.

evidence.supports: Dated slides contrast Tofu1 and Tofu2 and describe chip integration and network topology.

date.basis: JAXA dates the first operational SORA-MA configuration to phase 2 in April 2015.

events.statement: Tofu2 entered operation at JAXA in the initial PRIMEHPC FX100 SORA-MA configuration.

evidence.locator: Overview of JSS2, phase 2 and phase 3
evidence.supports: The operator dates operation of a partial SORA-MA configuration to April 2015.
Identifies the SORA-MA FX100 and its installed Tofu2 interconnect.

date.basis: The NIFS announcement dates the updated system's start of operation to 1 June.

events.statement: Tofu2 entered operation in the Fujitsu PRIMEHPC FX100 installed for the updated Plasma Simulator at NIFS in Toki, Gifu.

evidence.supports: The institute identifies the system and dates operation at its location.
The independent benchmark list identifies the NIFS installation's Tofu2 interconnect.
The designers identify Tofu2 as the FX100 interconnect.

earliest_record.rationale: The dated designer presentation establishes the public design account. The NIFS installation dates a subsequent deployed instance.

research.note: JAXA's deployed-system account corroborates the topology and controller placement Fujitsu described. Measurements on the operating generations demonstrate software behavior under particular configurations.

unresolved.about: Implementation details across the first two generations
unresolved.note: Which routing, virtual topology mapping and barrier implementation details were preserved? The MPI locking benchmark compared different implementations and tests use of a newly documented Tofu2 capability.

places.note: Documented in the JAXA SORA-MA and NIFS Plasma Simulator deployments.

links.statement: Fujitsu retained the original Tofu’s six-dimensional mesh/torus in Tofu2 and moved the network controller from a separate chip into the FX100’s processor.
links.scope: Six-dimensional network topology and controller integration from K and FX10 to FX100.

evidence.supports: The designer identifies Tofu2 as the next generation and specifies the six named axes and integration of the controller.

evidence.locator: P. 1, opening paragraphs and system diagram
evidence.supports: The FX10 customer identifies its installed original Tofu network as a six-dimensional mesh/torus.
The FX100 operator identifies the system's inheritance from K and FX10 and describes its deployed six-dimensional mesh/torus and integrated controller.

links.statement: Beyond the topology, which original Tofu routing, hardware-barrier and rank-mapping details deployed in K carried into Tofu2?
links.scope: Remaining implementation-level questions across K, FX10 and FX100.
links.finding: A separate design-to-design link records the supported continuity of the six-dimensional mesh/torus and the controller integration change. Which routing, hardware-barrier and rank-mapping internals carried over remains open.

evidence.supports: Fujitsu credits K’s original Tofu and identifies network topology as retained and integration as the generational change.
The report names K and FX100 as the earlier deployed Tofu generations. Its technical comparison closely follows the Fujitsu account.
JAXA verifies the FX100 topology and controller placement in service and describes system-level inheritance. Its measurements concern application performance.
The benchmark verifies the use of new Tofu2 atomic operations and compares two distinct software implementations.
